recentItems.description: Attorney Drew Findling discussed the complexities of representing rapper Lil Durk in a federal case. The indictment involves unreleased music allegedly monetizing violence. Findling argues the incriminating evidence, including song edits, involves fan-generated content unrelated to Durk. A motion to dismiss the case, citing misinformation potentially presented to the grand jury, is set for hearing, with significant implications depending on its outcome. Durk's family criticizes this use of lyrics in legal proceedings, emphasizing artistic expression and societal implications.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Chingy reacts to Lil Durk’s ongoing murder-for-hire case connected to the Los Angeles shooting that killed Lul Pab, cousin of Quando Rondo. Chingy recalls landing in LA and driving past the gas station across from the Beverly Center shortly after the incident, noting how shocking it was to see violence erupt in such a high-profile area near Beverly Hills. He and DJ Vlad discuss alleged associates testifying, the dangers of bringing street conflicts into the music business, and why successful artists must separate from destructive environments. Chingy also speaks on what he calls “genocide rap,” his shift toward “Luxury Midwestern Soul,” and the broader pattern of rapper deaths involving figures like Nipsey Hussle, Young Dolph, Takeoff, Mo3, FBG Duck, Gangsta Boo, Mac Miller, and Coolio. A candid conversation on hip-hop, fame, street violence, and survival.

--------
Nicholas Irving joins Shawn Prez for a blunt VladTV discussion on U.S. intelligence, Iran’s nuclear program, and the echoes of the Iraq War. Reacting to Robert O’Neill’s doubts about claims that Iran was “weeks away” from a nuclear weapon, Irving says he believes much of the war-related intel fed to the public is propaganda, comparing current Iran narratives to the failed weapons of mass destruction claims used to justify Iraq. He also references Joe Kent and intelligence agencies that allegedly questioned the Trump administration’s timeline, while discussing the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement under President Obama and whether politics influenced later decisions. The conversation expands into Trump’s reputation for pettiness, foreign policy, and a viral social media debate involving Cuban American Trump supporters and deportations to Africa. A candid exchange on war, power, media narratives, and public trust.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/K7__iCx2ghE
--------
Defense attorney Bradford Cohen joins Vlad to discuss why lawyers often avoid interviews during active cases, referencing Vlad’s conversation with Arthur Horne, attorney for Big30. Cohen explains the risks of speaking publicly before trial, how outside audiences often judge cases from limited clips, and why legal strategy can differ from public perception. The conversation turns to the controversial video allegedly showing Pooh Shiesty robbing Gucci Mane at gunpoint, with Cohen saying he believes the footage was “most definitely” leaked by people connected to the federal case. He also compares the situation to the Diddy and Cassie hotel video, offering his view on who may have released it and why. Cohen breaks down how federal prosecutors use press releases, witness pressure, and public information to advance cases, arguing that leaks and aggressive tactics are part of the reality of federal court.

--------

In this VladTV conversation, Max B revisits a pivotal period in his Dipset-era career, from contributions to Jim Jones’ *Hustler’s P.O.M.E.* and songs involving Cam’ron and Juelz Santana to the events that later shaped his criminal case. The Harlem rapper discusses meeting Gina Conway in Myrtle Beach, their relationship in New York, her work at Sin City in the Bronx, and her testimony about Allen Plowden, a Fort Lee Holiday Inn, and a reported $30,000 Louis Vuitton bag. Vlad also presses Max B on allegations that he connected Conway with his codefendant Kelvin Lillard, aka Pooh Simms, before a robbery prosecutors said led to murder. Max B challenges parts of the narrative, discusses hearsay, his legal defense, serving 18 years, and why he says his lawyer’s failures changed the outcome.

--------
Mario Sanchez sits down with Vlad to discuss major California gang indictments, prison politics, and the realities of speaking publicly as a former Norteño. The conversation covers the January 6 federal racketeering case tied to Salinas and the Coastal Plaza Norteño, including allegations of 11 murders, 14 attempted murders, dues paid to Nuestra Familia, and the reported punishment for leaving. Sanchez also reacts to Raul Coronel Suarez’s 30-year RICO sentence and explains why large cases often lead to informants and crews collapsing.

The interview also touches on Southern California’s Mexican Mafia crackdown, alleged tax collection, extortion, fentanyl and meth trafficking, and prison “big homie” structure. Sanchez addresses today’s Norteño-Sureño dynamics, prison truces, podcasts, and social media “woofing,” including online threats and comments calling him a dropout—while reflecting on doing time in the 1990s versus the internet era.

recentItems.title: Vlad Reacts to Lil Durk Being Found Not Guilty on All Charges
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
VladTV’s Vlad the Butcher responds to Lil Durk’s not guilty verdict, breaking down why the jury may have found reasonable doubt in the murder-for-hire case tied to Quando Rondo and the death of Lil Pop. Vlad discusses the prosecution’s evidence, including witnesses, text messages, phone records, alleged payments, and why he believes there was “no smoking gun” directly linking Durk to an order.

He also examines the role of Durk’s defense team, including Drew Findling and Brian Steele, and questions the credibility of cooperating witnesses such as OTF Jam and OTF Vonnie, who were facing serious prison time. The segment also touches on King Von, Lil Tim, Trap Lore Ross, possible civil litigation, and the emotional fallout for everyone involved.

A measured reaction to a closely watched hip-hop legal case, with condolences to Lil Pop’s family and perspective on the cost of street conflicts.
